rows.title: Dashboard tabs declare the ARIA tab pattern without its keyboard model
rows.scenario: In the generated mission-control widget, focus the “execution detail” tab and press ArrowRight (or Home/End) → focus and selection do not move to the other tab because the controls only handle click, both tabs remain in the ordinary Tab sequence, and the associated panels have neither role=tabpanel nor aria-controls linkage.
rows.fix: Implement the complete ARIA tabs pattern: roving tabindex, Left/Right and Home/End navigation with focus/selection synchronization, and explicit tab-to-tabpanel relationships; otherwise remove the tab roles and use ordinary buttons with honest semantics.

rows.title: Dependency-graph nodes are exposed as buttons but cannot be activated from the keyboard
rows.scenario: Open a generated dependency graph, Tab to a module or component circle, and press Enter or Space → no activation occurs because the only keydown behavior handles Escape, even though each SVG circle declares role=button and click opens its details.
rows.fix: Prefer a native keyboard-operable control associated with each SVG node, or implement Enter and Space activation (including preventDefault for Space) for both module and component nodes; if focus alone is the intended behavior, expose a non-button semantic instead.

rows.title: Terminal truth has no production composition root
rows.scenario: A governed run reaches its terminal stage and the individual checkpoint, report, repository, and release adapters prepare their projections, but no non-test caller constructs TerminalCoordinator or invokes prepare_delivery, commit_delivery, and reconcile_delivery. No CAS-backed terminal receipt is therefore produced, while repository.guard_terminal_delivery requires that live receipt, so the delivery cannot become terminal through the shipped CLI or loop path.
rows.fix: Add one orchestrator-only production composition path that assembles the eight surfaces, owns the coordinator lifecycle, commits and reconciles the exact-SHA bundle, and passes the resulting live authority receipt to Done and delivery guards. Exercise that path end to end rather than only constructing the coordinator in tests.

rows.title: A process restart permanently loses terminal-finalization authority
rows.scenario: The orchestrator creates issuer.json and then the process dies before or after the CAS. A restarted process can read only the issuer fingerprint; the matching OrchestratorIssuer secret/object was intentionally never serialized, so _bind_orchestrator_issuer returns None and issue_capability refuses the retry. The advertised crash-recovery path is thus unavailable after the failure mode it is meant to handle.
rows.fix: Introduce a durable, restart-safe orchestrator rebind mechanism tied to the governed run and authority root, or move capability custody to a host authority that can reissue it after authenticated recovery. Add a true subprocess-restart test that completes both pre-CAS retry and post-CAS reconciliation without retaining a Python object from the failed process.

rows.title: Immutable evidence is written directly to its final path
rows.scenario: The process is killed after os.open(O_EXCL) creates bundle.json or a surface file but before the write and fsync finish. The final path remains with truncated bytes; the next idempotent commit sees that the path exists and raises an immutable evidence collision, leaving an unpublished pre-CAS delivery unable to retry without manual deletion.
rows.fix: Write immutable bytes to a unique temporary file in the same directory, fsync it, atomically link or rename it into the content-addressed final name with collision verification, and fsync the parent directory. Cover a real mid-write process kill and recovery, not only fault injection after a complete write.

rows.title: Evidence-store CAS admits two successors for one predecessor
rows.scenario: Two Taskplane processes prepare different evidence operations against the same domain HEAD H and then commit concurrently. Both read H at line 496 and pass the predecessor check before either writes; each persists its immutable receipt and replaces HEAD/STATE, so both callers can report success while the last writer wins and two receipts claim the same predecessor. The fixed HEAD.tmp and STATE.tmp names add a second race in which one writer can rename the other writer's temporary bytes or fail after its peer removes the shared temp path.
rows.fix: Serialize the complete read-check-receipt-write-HEAD/STATE transaction with a per-domain cross-process lock, re-read and validate HEAD while holding that lock, and use unique same-directory temporary names. The losing successor must receive a CAS conflict and no committed-success response.

rows.title: Stage commits can permanently omit their run-journal event
rows.scenario: A stage operation atomically replaces manifest.json and then the process is killed or journal.jsonl becomes unwritable before _append_journal completes. Retrying the same operation finds the stored operation receipt at lines 681-692 and returns it immediately, so the missing journal event is never re-driven even though the stage head and revision advanced. Terminal reconciliation can therefore observe committed stage state whose required run-journal surface omits that lifecycle transition.
rows.fix: Commit a keyed journal outbox entry in the same manifest transaction as the stage mutation, then relay it idempotently to journal.jsonl and mark delivery. Replay and startup reconciliation must deliver a missing event before returning the stored operation receipt.

rows.title: Producer authority is consumed before any durable observation intent
rows.scenario: A Codex SubagentStop reaches observe_submission, consumes its process-private one-use capability, and then evidence_store.prepare fails before the intent is durably written (for example, permission loss or disk exhaustion). The hook wrapper completes that claimed stop with an error/block response, duplicate hook paths replay the response instead of executing again, and the consumed capability cannot be reused; the required producer observation is absent and lifecycle completion stays blocked with no executable reconciliation input.
rows.fix: Persist a claim-bound observation intent before consuming the one-use capability, or atomically couple capability consumption to the evidence transaction. Keep failed hook claims retryable by stable hook_claim_id and add an idempotent startup/duplicate-hook reconciliation path that can finish the exact stored intent without reminting authority.

rows.title: Python CI has no lint or strict type-check gate
rows.scenario: A contributor adds an unresolved name, stale suppression, untyped public API, or return-type mismatch that still parses and is not exercised by tests; the current Python job only compiles/imports and runs pytest, so CI reports success for code the pinned Python quality gate requires ruff and strict mypy or pyright to reject.
rows.fix: Add configured ruff lint/format and strict mypy or pyright checks to CI, with the pinned strictness settings and zero-warning enforcement.

rows.title: Native authority validator is shipped but never wired into production
rows.scenario: A Design or Plan omits or weakens the seven-capability Codex-native authority map; direct unit tests prove validate_design_and_plan would reject it, but no production module imports or calls native_authority, so the live Design/Plan path never executes this fail-closed validator and can proceed without the promised boundary check.
rows.fix: Invoke validate_design_and_plan and validate_delivery_roots from the authoritative Design/Plan gate before Build, and add an integration test that severs that production call and observes the gate fail.

rows.title: Design sweep validator is a dead production surface
rows.scenario: A retained Design sweep is missing a lens, runs serially, uses deep mode, or lacks a disposition; validate_design_sweep rejects those cases in its direct tests, but production code never imports or calls design_sweep, so the Design gate cannot enforce the documented 26-lens quick concurrent sweep contract.
rows.fix: Wire validate_design_sweep into the authoritative Design evidence gate and add a production-path integration test that fails when the validator is disconnected.

rows.title: Working preview production entry points are never wired into a live flow
rows.scenario: A Design, Build, or dynamic Review reaches the point where a working preview should launch; launch_design_preview, launch_build_preview, and launch_dynamic_review_preview are declared as the production entries, but no non-test production module imports or calls them, so the flow cannot register, open, or return the implemented preview and the feature remains reachable only from test_host_preview_runtime.py.
rows.fix: Call the flow-specific launch entry from the authoritative Design, Build, and dynamic Review orchestration paths with the required authorization and capability inputs, and add integration tests that fail when each production edge is severed; otherwise remove the misleading production surface.

rows.title: Standalone reviews have no enforced token ceiling by default
rows.scenario: Start a standalone review without --max-tokens on a large change -> the contract advertises the default $3 max_cost_usd value, but that value is only a cooperative stop signal and every generated deep-lens contract is bounded only by 45 tool actions -> up to eight deep agents plus the sweep can keep consuming model input, reasoning, and output tokens with no spend-proportional ceiling; prompt size and tokens per action multiply the actual cost while the displayed dollar value never blocks execution.
rows.fix: Give standalone review and each generated lens contract a finite default effective-token ceiling, propagate any caller override into producer contracts, and enforce that ceiling before further model/tool work; present max_cost_usd as advisory rather than as a budget ceiling unless the host can enforce it.

rows.title: Critical state writes are acknowledged before they are durable
rows.scenario: Run a state-changing command such as a loop gate or requirement update on a filesystem with delayed writeback, let atomic_write_json return after os.replace, and then lose power before dirty data and directory metadata reach stable storage -> after reboot the target can contain old, missing, or incomplete state even though the command reported success, rolling back gate, contract, requirement, or audit authority.
rows.fix: Flush and os.fsync the temporary file before replacement, then fsync the containing directory after os.replace; use collision-safe temporary names and add fault-injection coverage for crashes before and after each durability boundary.

rows.title: Interrupted cross-filesystem KB migration makes a partial copy authoritative
rows.scenario: Put the checkout's knowledge directory and TASKPLANE_HOME on different filesystems, then exhaust the destination or interrupt shutil.move during its copy fallback -> a partial external knowledge directory remains while the complete source is still present; the next migration skips because the destination directory exists, and kb_root prefers that partial destination, hiding source-only decisions and history.
rows.fix: Copy into a unique staging directory on the destination filesystem, fsync and verify a complete file manifest or checksums, atomically rename the verified staging directory into place, and only then remove the source; on retry, detect and reconcile or quarantine partial destinations instead of treating directory existence as completion.

rows.title: Fallback dashboard actions are inert
rows.scenario: A host has no native widget API, so Taskplane renders this documented fallback surface -> the user clicks an inline safe action such as approve, a detail action such as inspect, or Send in the retained composer -> the only emitted controller handles opening and closing the details dialog, so the action produces no message, progress state, error, or recovery path (and the form falls through to default browser submission).
rows.fix: Bind primary and detail actions plus the composer to the host chat bridge, and use the existing static-view pattern to reveal an exact reply when no bridge exists; show pending, confirmed, and failed-with-retry states instead of leaving active-looking controls dead.

rows.title: The fallback dashboard drops the workflow evidence it is meant to present
rows.scenario: A review snapshot contains finding or criterion items, including more than one carousel page -> the fallback renders only the component name, generic status, provenance, and text such as '9 items; page 1 of 2' -> none of the current-page items are shown, there are no previous/next controls, and the full-screen detail dialog contains only action buttons and a 1x1 placeholder image, so the user cannot inspect the evidence before acting.
rows.fix: Render each component's semantic value and the active carousel page in its card or full-screen detail, add visible previous/next controls driven by the projection's navigation metadata, and preserve stable item identity and filters while paging.

rows.title: Gate actions claim success before the chat bridge confirms delivery
rows.scenario: The OpenAI chat bridge exists but sendFollowUpMessage rejects because the connection drops -> tpFire immediately disables every gate choice and replaces the selected label with 'approved', 'signed off', or another terminal-looking result before calling the bridge -> there is no promise/error handling, so the user sees false success and has no retry or alternate action without re-rendering the dashboard.
rows.fix: Show a nonterminal sending state while the bridge request is in flight, apply the terminal label only after confirmed delivery, and on failure restore all choices with an inline explanation and retry/copy-to-chat recovery.

rows.title: Marketplace packaging bypasses the release-authority gate
rows.scenario: A maintainer checks out a clean commit whose CI or terminal release evidence is red, runs the documented package command, and uploads the resulting archive; the packager accepts it because provenance validates only the source commit and dirty state, even though taskplane/release_evidence.py requires a validated release-green receipt, fresh protected-platform proof, outside-model human recheck, and exact terminal authority before publication.
rows.fix: Make publication consume an immutable CI-built artifact that is bound to the validated release-green and terminal-authority receipts for the same SHA, or require and validate those receipts directly in a release-only packaging mode; update the portal checklist so a locally rebuilt archive cannot be the publication input without that gate.

rows.title: Host-native dashboard actions and composer are rendered without behavior
rows.scenario: Render a host-native dashboard snapshot with safe_actions=("approve", "decline"), then click Approve or type a message and submit the retained composer -> the action button has only a data-action attribute, the controller binds only the optional Details dialog, and the form has no submit handler, so no follow-up is sent and the workflow remains awaiting approval (the form may also perform a default page submission).
rows.fix: Bind every primary/detail action and the composer to the host message bridge in the fallback/reference controller, with explicit pending, success, and recoverable error states; if this surface is intentionally presentation-only, render these affordances as non-interactive text instead of actionable controls.

rows.title: Gate controls claim success before the asynchronous chat bridge succeeds
rows.scenario: Open a mission-control widget in a host where window.openai.sendFollowUpMessage exists but returns a rejected promise (for example, the bridge disconnects during an approval click) -> tpFire immediately disables every gate choice and replaces the selected label with a checkmark, while tpSend neither awaits nor catches the promise, leaving the user with a false success state and no retry or error path although the approval message was never delivered.
rows.fix: Make the send path promise-aware: enter a labelled pending state, await bridge completion, mark success only after fulfillment, and on rejection restore all valid controls with an announced error and retry path; handle a synchronous bridge result through the same normalized promise flow.

rows.title: Release compatibility gate skips the last released generation
rows.scenario: A user running the last released plugin generation 2.17.20 upgrades to candidate 2.17.25 -> the mandatory mixed-version proof exercises only 2.17.25 and superseded, never-released 2.17.24 cells -> an incompatibility in persisted state, receipts, hooks, or host/plugin exchange between the production release and the candidate can pass release-green without being observed.
rows.fix: Define the release compatibility window from the last actually released generation (2.17.20) and require mixed plugin/host plus persisted-state migration coverage for 2.17.20 <-> 2.17.25; if 2.17.24 remains useful as a development boundary, test it as an additional candidate cell rather than substituting it for the production predecessor.

rows.title: Durable command logs retain personal data verbatim
rows.scenario: Against the empty-tree baseline, this diff adds command-output persistence that redacts only credential-shaped secrets; when a governed test or build prints an email address, customer name, health detail, or other personal data, append_output writes it unchanged to artifacts/output.log and keeps the same text in the event summary with no retention limit or downstream purge path.
rows.fix: Classify command output as potentially personal data, minimise it before persistence, add configurable PII redaction or a metadata-only default, and implement a bounded retention/purge mechanism that removes the artifact and every summary copy.

rows.title: Canonical review artifacts keep raw diffs indefinitely
rows.scenario: Against the empty-tree baseline, a review of a change containing a person's email, support transcript, precise location, or other personal data stores the complete patch in the content-addressed diff artifact; ArtifactStore is immutable and tp gc explicitly excludes governance records, so completing or cleaning up the review leaves this additional raw-data copy without a TTL or review-scoped deletion mechanism.
rows.fix: Minimise or redact personal data before persisting review evidence, document an accountable retention period, and add an attributable review/run purge that deletes raw diff artifacts and all derived copies while retaining only non-content fingerprints needed for audit.

rows.title: Append-only audit traces accept unsanitized identity and free-text fields
rows.scenario: Against the empty-tree baseline, trace() copies arbitrary caller data directly into trace.jsonl; existing callers pass human approver strings, goals, decision titles, tags, commands, and error text. If those values identify a person or contain incident/customer details, rotation deliberately preserves every generation forever and no privacy redaction or expiry removes them.
rows.fix: Replace free-form trace payloads with an allowlisted, minimised schema; pseudonymise actor identities, redact personal content at the sink, and enforce a documented retention cap with deletion across active and rotated trace files.

rows.title: Release gate skips the last released production generation
rows.scenario: A user running the documented last released generation 2.17.20 upgrades one side of the host/plugin pair to 2.17.25 during the declared emit-before-require rollout -> the only required matrix covers 2.17.25 and superseded, never-released 2.17.24, so the real 2.17.25/2.17.20 mixed state is untested and compatibility_cell rejects it as an unknown generation; nevertheless a complete four-cell 2.17.25/2.17.24 receipt can satisfy the release prerequisite without proving the production upgrade path.
rows.fix: Make the last released generation (2.17.20) an explicit supported predecessor in the rollout/deprecation window and require observed mixed host/plugin cells against it before release, or define and verify an atomic upgrade that makes mixed 2.17.25/2.17.20 states impossible; keep 2.17.24 only as an additional candidate-compatibility row rather than the sole N-1 release gate.

rows.title: Every screened action reparses the growing transcript twice
rows.scenario: A long governed Codex or Claude task accumulates a 100 MB transcript and then runs another shell or file action; `cmd_screen` reads the entire JSONL through `read_transcript` and immediately reads it again through `read_provider_transcript`, even when the active contract has no token ceiling, so each action performs roughly 200 MB of parsing and cumulative screening work grows quadratically with the number of turns.
rows.fix: Maintain an incremental usage checkpoint keyed by transcript identity, inode, size, and last parsed offset; parse only appended complete records, reset safely on truncation or replacement, share the normalized totals between ceiling enforcement and telemetry, and skip ceiling work entirely when neither a token budget nor usage telemetry consumer requires it.

rows.title: Review actions scan every historical host transcript
rows.scenario: A workstation has thousands of archived Codex and Claude sessions and the operator approves dynamic validation; `_host_review_action_receipt` recursively enumerates both complete session trees and reads up to 8 MB from every transcript to find one receipt, while `_host_review_execution_receipt` repeats the same global scan for the tool result, turning a single review gate into gigabytes of unrelated I/O and potentially making sign-off time out.
rows.fix: Bind the review run to its host-owned task or session locator when consent is observed, resolve an explicit receipt reference through a bounded index, and scan backward only within that one transcript with a strict byte or record limit; never recursively search unrelated historical sessions on the approval path.

rows.title: Preview startup materializes and hashes an unbounded workspace
rows.scenario: A repository contains a large untracked dependency tree, generated artifacts, or one multi-gigabyte file and a design, build, or dynamic-review preview starts; registration copies every top-level entry except `.git`, then fingerprints the sandbox and source multiple times (including the source `.git` tree once), with each file loaded wholly by `read_bytes`, before the preview lifetime, CPU, or memory controls are armed, so startup can exhaust disk or memory and never reach the bounded preview process.
rows.fix: Create previews from a pinned tracked-file manifest or explicit allowlist, enforce file-count, per-file-size, total-byte, and materialization-time budgets before copying, stream file hashes in bounded chunks, exclude VCS and generated dependency trees consistently, and fail with a structured unavailable outcome when any bound is exceeded.

rows.title: Read-only contracts allow opaque build and test launchers to mutate reviewed source
rows.scenario: A reviewed repository supplies a Makefile whose default test target overwrites src/app.py, and a reviewer runs make test under a Taskplane read-only contract. The command analyzer recognizes neither a concrete write target nor an opaque executor for make, pytest, tox, npm, or other console entry points, so the hook allows the command and the child process can modify the reviewed checkout despite the read-only contract.
rows.fix: Enforce read-only review commands with an operating-system filesystem boundary, or fail closed for every unrecognized executable and permit only a narrow direct-argv allowlist of proven read-only commands. Add regression cases for make, pytest, tox, npm, and repository-defined console scripts that attempt an out-of-scope write.

rows.title: The accepted architecture map has no executable graph consumer
rows.scenario: The Design DoD says strict scans consume design/contract.json#/architecture_decomposition and prove the three new owners are singleton SCCs with every declared edge, but the repository's only owner declaration is deliberately placed under an unknown components.yaml section that the parser ignores. Run the shipped graph path against this checkout: it consumes only floors and exclude, never architecture_decomposition or owners, so a forbidden dependency added to native_authority.py, design_sweep.py, or terminal_truth.py can leave the claimed graph DoD green because the required component identities and edges were never realized.
rows.fix: Implement one versioned, tested graph input for the approved architecture_decomposition map (or remove the claim and redesign the DoD around evidence the scanner actually emits); make final graph validation fail unless every declared node, SCC property, and proposed edge is realized at the candidate SHA.

rows.title: The exact-SHA terminal bundle no longer describes the main-integration candidate
rows.scenario: The only committed terminal projection names 106af4631ab5b5c041055b9b9b918d78a18ae50b and a full-suite fingerprint from that SHA, while the reviewed HEAD and origin/main are 00cd4f2c8183e57b6eae3f0cb6b0c580e00fe085 after two later commits that changed runtime and release surfaces. A consumer following the Design's terminal authority therefore either rejects the current v2.17.25 candidate as stale or, if it trusts the repository's candidate claim, accepts evidence for different bytes; the post-CAS rollback rule explicitly requires a successor bundle for a new candidate SHA.
rows.fix: Treat every post-finalization commit as a new candidate: rerun the complete final-SHA validation required by AC7 and append/reconcile a successor eight-surface bundle bound to 00cd4f2, or withdraw the main-integration/terminal-complete claim until that bundle exists.

rows.title: The design declares native token budgets enforceable on a host that exposes no token totals
rows.scenario: AC6 requires observed_tokens to be finite and non-null throughout the production wave and missing data to stop further dispatch, but the final receipt records host token telemetry as unavailable and budget_claim=false while README.md still says v2.17.25 completes sealed native dispatch and budget evidence. With the same host capability, a wave can exceed the 150M total or 25M uncached-input ceiling without Taskplane being able to measure the breach, so the promised acceptance validation cannot run and completion relies on an out-of-contract bypass instead.
rows.fix: Redesign AC6 around a provider capability the supported host actually exposes: either require an authenticated usage source before admitting a budget-governed wave, or define and obtain explicit human approval for a distinct no-token-budget mode whose outcome cannot satisfy or be advertised as AC6 completion.

rows.title: Validation-sandbox preparation can block forever
rows.scenario: A repository uses a slow or stuck Git LFS/smudge filter, or its local partial clone must hydrate an object while `prepare_review_validation_sandbox` runs `git clone`/`git checkout`; none of the preparation subprocesses has a timeout, so the review command never records a failure or returns control and the operator remains indefinitely stuck before dynamic validation.
rows.fix: Run every sandbox-preparation Git subprocess behind one bounded deadline with process-tree termination and cancellation propagation; classify timeout separately, clean the temporary checkout, and persist a structured failed-validation outcome that the operator can retry.

rows.title: Mission-control status indicators pulse indefinitely with no reduced-motion or pause path
rows.scenario: A user with reduced-motion enabled opens the standalone mission-control dashboard → the live indicator and current-step indicator continue pulsing every 1.2–1.4 seconds forever because the page defines infinite animations but no prefers-reduced-motion override or user control.
rows.fix: Disable the pulse under prefers-reduced-motion and provide a static non-motion status cue; if animation remains for other users, provide a way to pause it when it is not essential.

rows.title: The accepted architecture decomposition is not an input to any scanner
rows.scenario: A future change makes terminal_truth.py import a transition adapter, violating the required singleton-SCC boundary. The strict graph scan still reads components.yaml and the ordinary inferred decomposition only; no production or CI code reads design/contract.json#/architecture_decomposition, so the declared owner boundary can drift while the aggregate taskplane graph remains green.
rows.fix: Wire the accepted decomposition document into the strict graph path or materialize the same nodes and path globs in the scanner's supported component configuration, then compare realized nodes, SCCs, and semantic edges against the declared map in CI.

rows.title: New bare type-ignore suppressions hide the compatibility import boundary
rows.scenario: The fallback direct-import branch contains two bare type-ignore comments without error codes or reasons; when the imported interface changes or the suppression becomes stale, a type checker cannot distinguish the intended compatibility exception from an unrelated hidden error and the escape hatch remains silently green.
rows.fix: Type the compatibility import path correctly, or use narrowly coded ignores with an explicit reason and enable warn_unused_ignores so stale suppressions fail.

rows.title: A routing import failure disables the deep-agent cost cap
rows.scenario: Run breadth=all after lens_signals becomes unavailable or raises during import -> _deep_cap returns 0, which _cap_deep_dispatch interprets as no cap -> the whole-codebase review can fan out all 26 deep agents instead of the intended maximum of eight, multiplying model-session spend by up to 3.25x precisely while the cost-control dependency is degraded.
rows.fix: Fail closed for spend: use a validated engine-owned fallback ceiling or stop deep dispatch and require repair/human scope approval when the cap cannot be loaded; keep inline coverage if desired, but never interpret cap lookup failure as unlimited subagent fan-out.

rows.title: Every component state is visually presented as success
rows.scenario: A component value reports status 'failed', 'blocked', 'pending', or 'unavailable' -> the renderer always prefixes it with the same check mark and styles it with the single green status token -> an error or waiting state reads as successful even though the status word says otherwise, and no state-specific next action is surfaced.
rows.fix: Map the finite component states to distinct icon, label, and token combinations; reserve the check treatment for completed/ready states and pair failed or blocked states with their available recovery action.

rows.title: Pull-request jobs retain checkout credentials they never use
rows.scenario: A same-repository or private-repository pull request changes a test or packaging script executed by tests-portability, validate-plugin, docs-truth, codex-parity, or codex-host; because those checkout steps omit persist-credentials: false, the untrusted script can read and exfiltrate the job's contents-read GitHub token from Git configuration even though no later step needs Git authentication.
rows.fix: Set persist-credentials: false on every checkout that does not perform an authenticated Git operation, especially every pull-request-exposed job, and grant any exceptional credential at the narrow step that consumes it.

rows.title: CI resolves an unlocked test dependency on every run
rows.scenario: Two runs of the same commit occur before and after a new pytest 8.x wheel is published or an existing transitive artifact changes; pip install pytest==8.* resolves different bytes, so the later run can fail or execute different supply-chain code even though the repository and workflow are unchanged.
rows.fix: Declare the development toolchain in project metadata, commit a lock or hashed constraints file, and install that exact verified set in every CI job and in the contributor instructions.

rows.title: Dashboard copy has no locale-backed translation path
rows.scenario: Run Taskplane for a non-English user: the dashboard's catalog is explicitly English-only, while substantial UI chrome is also embedded directly in renderer functions, so changing the user's locale cannot produce a translated dashboard and translators cannot supply a BCP 47 fallback bundle.
rows.fix: Introduce a locale resolver with BCP 47 fallback, move every user-visible dashboard string (including aria labels and backend-generated status text) into complete message resources, and retain English as the explicit default locale.

rows.title: Plural evaluator can express only English one/other rules
rows.scenario: Translate a counted dashboard message into Arabic, Polish, Russian, or Welsh and render counts such as 0, 2, 3, or 11: the regex accepts only one and other branches and _msg selects solely on n == 1, so the locale's zero/two/few/many category cannot be represented and the rendered noun form is wrong.
rows.fix: Delegate plural selection to a CLDR/ICU-capable formatter keyed by the active locale, preserving full-message templates and all locale-required cardinal categories.

rows.title: Privacy notice denies data collection and third-party network use that the code performs
rows.scenario: A user relies on the notice saying taskplane collects no personal information, initiates no network requests, and integrates with no third party, but review flows require and persist an actor identity and invoke GitHub CLI/git fetch for PR metadata and repository content. The user therefore cannot learn from the notice what identifiers and repository data are processed, their purpose and retention, or that GitHub receives request metadata under its own terms.
rows.fix: Replace the categorical denials with an accurate data-flow inventory covering actor/approval identifiers, repository and command artifacts, Git/GitHub acquisition, purposes, storage locations, retention/deletion, accountable owner, and provider/transfer terms; scope any jurisdiction-specific commitments explicitly.

rows.title: A repository-controlled setting defaults a new user to shared storage
rows.scenario: A developer clones a team repository containing .taskplane-kb/config.json and has no personal mode record; the resolver immediately selects the committed in-repo store and merely emits a notice. If the developer records a decision containing a person's name or incident context before running share set private, the data is written into a team-visible, committable location without that developer actively choosing sharing.
rows.fix: Default each new local user to external/private storage until they explicitly confirm shared mode, or gate the first shared write on an attributable acknowledgement; keep share set private as a universal opt-out and make the pre-write destination visible.

rows.title: Primary journey describes approval checkpoints the current flow has consolidated
rows.scenario: A delivery lead reads the top-level Evaluate-Loop journey and plans for a Design approval followed by a separate plan approval, then starts a complex build and receives one consolidated Product/Design/Plan pre-implementation authorization packet instead; the documented journey and the actual decision cadence do not match.
rows.fix: Describe the current sequence as Product, optional Design, and Plan passing mechanical gates before one consolidated pre-implementation authorization, followed by final sign-off; reserve separate checkpoints only for explicitly exceptional decisions.

rows.title: Marketplace copy implies an actively executed full 26-lens review
rows.scenario: A buyer selects taskplane because the long description promises a full 26-lens engineering review, runs an ordinary review, and receives only the selectively routed deep set plus at most one light sweep while the remaining lenses are recorded as light or n/a dispositions; the phrase 'full 26-lens engineering review' overstates the active review work compared with the product's selective-routing contract.
rows.fix: Use one precise public phrase across the manifest, README, and submission worksheet: a complete 26-lens disposition with only the evidence-selected deep/light reviewers executed, and explain that n/a lenses are disclosed rather than run.

rows.title: Canonical design-sweep proof is optional in CI
rows.scenario: On a clean GitHub runner the hard-coded local Codex session file does not exist, so pytest skips the only test that binds the claimed 26-lens overlapping Design sweep to the retained real audit; a missing, corrupted, or no-longer-reproducible canonical audit therefore leaves the required suite green on synthetic fixtures alone.
rows.fix: Check in a sanitized content-addressed audit fixture or provision it in a required CI/release job, and fail that gate when the exact canonical bytes are unavailable instead of skipping.

rows.title: No required end-to-end Codex producer-event path
rows.scenario: When TASKPLANE_CODEX_PRODUCER_EVENT_FILE is absent (as in the declared codex-host CI job), the live canary exits as skipped; a Codex host integration change that stops emitting either evaluate or em producer observations can ship while all mandatory fixture and mocked-host checks remain green.
rows.fix: Add a required scheduled or release-bound live-host job that supplies an immutable capture from a real Codex run and treats a missing capture or missing evaluate/em events as failure; keep fixture tests as the deterministic lower layer.

rows.title: Publication-concurrency test orders threads with a fixed sleep
rows.scenario: On a loaded runner the loser thread can remain unscheduled for more than 100 ms; the test then releases the winner before the loser has actually attempted collection, so the loser may run after the reservation is released and produce a different outcome, intermittently failing a test intended to prove simultaneous publication exclusion.
rows.fix: Replace the sleep with deterministic synchronization: have the losing path signal that it has reached the reservation attempt (or inject a controllable barrier/clock), then release the winner and assert the ordered outcomes.

rows.title: CI repeatedly installs a moving pytest release without integrity hashes
rows.scenario: A future or compromised pytest 8.x release is selected by the pytest==8.* constraint in each CI job and executes before the repository tests. That package can alter test behavior or runner output, undermining the otherwise SHA-pinned workflow and allowing a false-green build without any repository change.
rows.fix: Resolve pytest and its transitive dependencies to exact reviewed versions with hashes, install them with hash enforcement from a committed lock or constraints file, and update that lock through an explicit dependency-review process.

rows.title: CI resolves an unsealed pytest dependency tree on every run
rows.scenario: A new pytest 8.x release or any newly selected transitive release is published, then an unchanged commit reruns CI and executes different third-party bytes because each of the six test jobs installs `pytest==8.*` without a lock file or hashes; the same source revision can therefore change from green to red, or consume a compromised transitive release, despite the workflow explicitly pinning GitHub Actions by full commit SHA.
rows.fix: Select one exact pytest release and seal its full transitive set with hashes in a dedicated development lock/constraints file; install that same file in every CI job and document the matching contributor command.

rows.title: Repository acquisition retries immediately and at two layers
rows.scenario: A provider returns repeated transient HTTP/2/RPC failures or throttles fetches; `_fetch` immediately retries once with HTTP/1.1 and `acquire_with_recovery` then immediately repeats the whole acquisition up to three times, potentially issuing six back-to-back 600-second fetch attempts and exhausting the retry budget before the provider can recover.
rows.fix: Make one layer own the retry budget, add capped exponential backoff with randomized jitter and Retry-After support, and enforce a single end-to-end acquisition deadline while retaining per-attempt telemetry.

rows.title: The no-network privacy promise no longer matches remote repository acquisition
rows.scenario: A user relies on the policy's categorical statement that the plugin initiates no network requests, then asks Taskplane to prepare or review a pull-request URL; repository acquisition invokes GitHub metadata access and `git fetch` (for example taskplane/repository.py:1087-1103), so the plugin-initiated workflow does contact a third party despite the published promise. The promise predates the remote-acquisition implementation (1416908 versus 0c3c5841).
rows.fix: Narrow the promise to no telemetry or author-operated service, and explicitly disclose the user-requested Git/GitHub and package-manager network operations, what data they send, and whose credentials and privacy terms govern them.

rows.title: The public prerequisite says Python 3 although the CLI requires Python 3.10+
rows.scenario: A user on Python 3.8 or 3.9 reads the Install section, satisfies the stated `Python 3` prerequisite, and starts Taskplane; taskplane/tp.py:29-40 immediately exits with status 2 because the enforced minimum is 3.10. The 3.10 floor was added later (470b5b2) without updating this older prerequisite (8089767).
rows.fix: State `CPython 3.10 or newer` in the README prerequisite and link to the validated 3.10-3.13 support matrix in docs/configuration.md.

rows.title: The loop command synopsis omits the supported `unavailable` outcome
rows.scenario: An evaluator encounters a proven host/model outage and consults the shipped loop synopsis; it lists only `pass|fail`, so the operator can submit `fail` and incorrectly consume a product fix cycle instead of using the parser-supported `unavailable` outcome at taskplane/tp.py:7285-7288. `unavailable` was added in 1556f88, after this synopsis was written.
rows.fix: Change the synopsis to `pass|fail|unavailable` and label `unavailable` as evaluator-only for a structured host/model outage, matching the canonical harness rule.

rows.title: Onboarding presents `tp init` as scaffolding but omits its legacy-KB migration side effect
rows.scenario: A brownfield user authorizes the documented initialization step expecting four new context files, a graph scan, and a knowledge base; `tp init` also moves an existing tracked `knowledge/` directory, runs `git rm --cached`, and edits `.gitignore` (taskplane/tp.py:4068-4081 and 4200-4212). That warning appears only later in docs/state-spec.md, after the step it governs.
rows.fix: Place a before-you-run warning directly under the onboarding step, summarize the exact move/untrack/ignore behavior, and link to the migration section before asking the user to authorize initialization.

rows.title: Importing the test package permanently rewires process-wide runner state
rows.scenario: A larger Python test process imports taskplane.tests and then runs unrelated tests: tempfile.tempdir and TMPDIR remain redirected, shutil.rmtree and unittest.TestCase.run remain monkey-patched, and the unrelated tests execute against Taskplane's session hooks with no teardown that restores the original process state.
rows.fix: Move the isolation into a runner-scoped context or bootstrap subprocess and restore every changed environment variable, module attribute, and class method in a guaranteed teardown; keep import of taskplane.tests side-effect free.

rows.title: Deferred P1/P2 work is not linked to priced debt records
rows.scenario: The first corrective wave deliberately ships only the four P0 controls and excludes all P1/P2 retrospective follow-ups, but the repository authority names those deferrals only as a group. When the next wave is prioritized, there is no linked record stating which follow-ups accumulated backfill, migration, compatibility, or operator re-teaching cost while waiting, so the team cannot compare the earlier-release payoff of this cut with its later repayment price and individual follow-ups can be lost or discovered only after their cost has grown.
rows.fix: Keep the current P0 vertical slice, but link each excluded P1/P2 follow-up to a tracked debt record that names its owner, re-entry trigger, and estimated now-versus-later repayment cost (including any backfill, migration, compatibility, or re-teaching work); reference those debt IDs from the Out of scope section.

rows.title: The terminal capability choice hides the recoverability it spends
rows.scenario: The selected design makes the orchestrator capability non-serializable and records only its fingerprint. If the root finalizer process restarts after issuer.json is created, the replacement process has no live issuer object and cannot obtain commit authority, so the promised idempotent reconciliation path is unavailable precisely after a crash. The alternatives table optimizes authority integrity and terminal reliability but never scores restart recoverability or operability against a reissuable host capability or a durably protected issuer.
rows.fix: Add the capability-custody choice to the proposed decision as a real trade-off: compare at least host-authenticated reissuance, a durably protected issuer, and process-only custody; name authority isolation gained versus restart recoverability spent; select an observable revisit trigger such as the first finalizer process replacement or a failed restart canary.

rows.title: The one-way stage migration has no alternatives or revisit trigger
rows.scenario: A workspace is atomically switched from the legacy singleton to stage authority and a later production defect is discovered in the v4 projection. Reversal requires restoring persistent control state across the loop, track, stage, and run-store modules, while the document explicitly says no reverse migration exists. The section specifies safeguards for the chosen one-way conversion but records neither a competent alternative such as dual-read shadowing or a reversible authority adapter nor an observable condition for reconsidering the irreversible cutover.
rows.fix: Record this as a proposed one-way-door decision with at least two implementable migration strategies, a gained/given-up table naming integrity versus rollback operability, and a measurable cutover/revisit rule such as a clean shadow-read period plus zero conservation mismatches across a stated number of migrated workspaces.

rows.title: Loop-engine ownership is locked in prose but absent from the decision registry
rows.scenario: A host adds native lifecycle authority and Taskplane must determine which scheduling and execution responsibilities to retain. The repository says the cross-module loop-engine ownership choice is locked and shipped, but the active decision registry is empty, so retrieval by affected module cannot surface the original criteria, alternatives, or supersession relationship; later work can silently narrow the ownership boundary and re-litigate it from code and prose alone.
rows.fix: Promote the shipped ownership choice into a versioned decision record with affected module globs, requirement provenance, the orchestrator-owned alternative and what it buys, the quality attributes gained and spent, and an observable revisit trigger tied to a stable host-native lifecycle capability; link any later boundary decision as a superseding or narrowing record.

rows.title: Small step metadata text misses WCAG AA contrast
rows.scenario: Render the standalone mission-control page → the 12px step metadata uses #77776c on #14140f, which measures 4.08:1 and falls below the 4.5:1 WCAG 1.4.3 threshold for normal text.
rows.fix: Use a lighter text token (or darker background) that reaches at least 4.5:1 in the shipped dark palette, then cover the exact foreground/background pair with a contrast assertion.

rows.title: Glob matching logic is deliberately duplicated across routing layers
rows.scenario: A future glob-semantics fix is applied to lens._match but not the copied graph_primitives._match; the same changed path then routes a lens differently from the dependency-graph detector even though both claim identical semantics.
rows.fix: Move the cycle-free matcher into a small dependency-neutral module and import it from both consumers, preserving focused parity tests.

rows.title: Visible finding text is truncated inside grapheme clusters
rows.scenario: Render a finding scenario whose 260th code point falls inside a family emoji ZWJ sequence, a combining-mark character, or a Devanagari cluster: the direct Python slice emits only part of the grapheme, so the dashboard displays a broken glyph even though the source finding is intact.
rows.fix: Truncate human-readable fields by Unicode grapheme cluster (or perform CSS visual truncation while retaining the full accessible value); apply the same helper to scenario, fix, goal, and decision-title display slices.

rows.title: Shared store metadata exposes workstation identity without minimisation
rows.scenario: When store migration runs while the resolved store is the in-repo team store, meta.json receives the absolute workspace path and realpath, commonly embedding the local account name, plus the Git remote. Committing .taskplane-kb then shares workstation-identifying data that is not needed for teammates to consume the decision registry.
rows.fix: Keep absolute paths in the external private locator only; write a pseudonymous project key and a normalized non-credentialed repository identity to shared metadata, or omit meta.json from the committable store entirely.

rows.title: The built-in tour presents v2.16 as the current release story
rows.scenario: A user upgrades or installs the 2.17.25 manifest and asks 'what's new'; tp-help leads with v2.16 and never introduces the intervening native-authority, zero-execution-lens, budget, real-checkout, and terminal-truth behavior that materially changes what the user should expect.
rows.fix: Make the tour's current-release section version-neutral and derive the current highlights from the manifest/changelog, or update and test it as part of every version bump so the help journey cannot lag the installed product.

rows.title: The declared sole development dependency omits Pillow
rows.scenario: A contributor follows the documented setup, which says pytest is the only development dependency, then attempts to regenerate the shipped README infographic with `scripts/render_readme_gif.py`; the script imports `PIL` and fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` in that documented environment, so a versioned release asset cannot be reproduced from the stated toolchain.
rows.fix: Declare the asset-generation toolchain separately from the runtime, pin Pillow in the development lock/constraints file, and document the exact regeneration command without adding Pillow to the stdlib-only runtime surface.

rows.title: The generated CLI reference drops allowed values for positional enums
rows.scenario: A reader looks up `tp.py loop submit`, `review signoff`, or `req signoff`; the reference names only generic positional arguments such as `outcome` or `decision`, while argparse restricts them to concrete choices such as `pass|fail|unavailable` and `approve|changes`. The reader cannot construct a valid command from the reference and must fall back to live `--help` or source code.
rows.fix: Teach the Markdown generator to render positional help, metavar, required/optional state, and `choices`, then regenerate docs/cli-reference.md and pin the behavior with a generator test.

rows.title: The complete generated CLI reference is not reachable from the documentation index
rows.scenario: A power user follows the README's `Going deeper` list to find command flags and outputs; it links specialist routes and configuration but not docs/cli-reference.md, and no other user-facing document links that generated reference. The only discovery path is browsing the repository tree or already knowing `tp help --md` exists.
rows.fix: Add the generated CLI reference to `Going deeper` and link it from the specialist-routes power-user section.

rows.title: The context-storage instructions contradict onboarding's four-document model
rows.scenario: A new user creates the four documented files (`product.md`, `tech-stack.md`, `workflow.md`, and `current-state.md`) and later reaches the context-storage section, which tells them to fill three context docs; they cannot tell which file is intentionally excluded and may leave `current-state.md` empty even though the earlier brownfield guidance makes it essential.
rows.fix: Use `four context docs` consistently and briefly state the reader question each file answers, with `current-state.md` first for brownfield repositories.

rows.title: Runtime dependency seams are mutable process singletons without scoped restoration
rows.scenario: Two tests or embedded orchestrators in one process bind different BUILD-C state loaders or wait factories: the later bind silently replaces the earlier process-global callbacks, so results depend on execution order and concurrent tests cannot use independent fakes.
rows.fix: Construct a per-run runtime-services object and pass it through the consuming boundary, or provide a context-managed binding that returns a restoration token and is safe for nested and parallel tests.
